instruction: Fresnel-driven Emission Ring `scene.blend` contains a UV sphere `Orb` (radius 1, default 32x16 segmentation) at the origin, shaded with a simple grey material `OrbMat` (Principled BSDF only, no emission). A camera at (0, -3, 0) looks along +Y at the orb (focal 50mm), and a single area light sits behind the camera. The scene renders with Cycles CPU (seed=0, samples=32, 256x256, denoiser on). Modify `OrbMat` so that the sphere gains a bright emission RING along its view-facing silhouette - i.e. A Fresnel-driven emission where grazing angles (the edges) glow and the centre stays dim. Wire a `ShaderNodeFresnel` so its output drives an emission contribution. A clean way is: Fresnel (IOR=1.45) -> Mix Shader factor, mixing the existing grey Principled BSDF with a cyan `ShaderNodeEmission` (color `(0.1, 1.0, 1.0)`, strength chosen so the ring is visibly bright). Equivalently, you can drive the Principled BSDF's Emission input with the Fresnel factor multiplied into a cyan color. Save the modified scene to `answer.blend`. Parameters - Emission color: `(0.1, 1.0, 1.0)` (bright cyan). - Fresnel IOR: 1.45 (the default). - Emission strength: scale so the ring is visibly bright (start around 2-3 and tune). Requirements: 1. `Orb` mesh exists at the origin with the same vertex count as in the init scene. 2. `OrbMat` uses nodes and contains a `ShaderNodeFresnel`. 3. `OrbMat` contains an emission pathway: either a `ShaderNodeEmission`, or the Principled BSDF's Emission input is driven. 4. The Fresnel node's output is connected (directly, or through a Mix Shader \ Math node) into the emission path. 5. When rendered with Cycles (seed=0, samples=32, 256x256, denoiser on), the rendered image satisfies: - Edge ROI (pixels with radius in [100, 120] from the image centre) has mean luma > 0.30. - Centre ROI (pixels with radius in [0, 30] from the image centre) has mean luma < 0.40. - Edge mean luma exceeds centre mean luma by at least 0.05. - On the edge ROI, mean B minus mean R > 0.10 (the rim is visibly cyan). Do not alter the orb's mesh, the camera, the light, or the render configuration - only `OrbMat` should change.
source: Schlick 1994 — "An Inexpensive BRDF Model for Physically-based Rendering", Eurographics
